source_excerpts.text:
## Model and quantifiers

Take any finite undirected graph with n fixed-temperature terminals and m
internal nodes. Each contact has a bounded, nonnegative, piecewise-continuous
P-periodic conductance. Write its symmetric graph Laplacian in blocks as

\[
 L(t)=\begin{pmatrix}D(t)&-B(t)^T\\-B(t)&A(t)\end{pmatrix}\succeq0.
\]

Internal temperatures x obey

\[
 C\dot x=-A(t)x+B(t)\theta,\qquad
 q(t)=D(t)\theta-B(t)^Tx,
 \tag{1}
\]

where theta is the constant terminal-temperature vector, q is heat current from
the terminals into the network, and C is a constant symmetric positive-definite
matrix. Ordinary lumped thermal capacities give diagonal C. There are no internal
heat sources, advection, temperature-dependent coefficients, hidden terminals,
or actuator heat/work in this ideal model. All results below hold for every
finite n,m, every such schedule, and every constant theta, subject to a unique
periodic solution. A connected averaged graph is a sufficient hypothesis.

Angle brackets denote one-period averages. Define

\[
 \bar A=\langle A\rangle,\quad\bar B=\langle B\rangle,\quad
 \bar D=\langle D\rangle,\quad X_*=\bar A^{-1}\bar B,
 \qquad Y_*=\bar D-\bar B^T\bar A^{-1}\bar B.
 \tag{2}
\]

Y_* is the established static Kron reduction of the **averaged contact graph**.
It is not the average of the instantaneous Kron reductions. Let x(t)=X(t)theta
be the periodic solution and define Y by average q=Y theta.

Existence detail: for an unforced solution,
\(\frac12\frac d{dt}(x^TCx)=-x^TA(t)x\leq0\).
If a nonzero state retained its C norm over a period, A(t)x(t)=0 almost
everywhere, hence x would be constant and lie in the kernel of bar A. With
bar A positive definite this is impossible. The period map has spectral radius
less than one, and the forced periodic solution is unique. Full connectivity of
the averaged graph also makes Y_* positive definite on the terminal-contrast
space \(\mathbf1^\perp\).

## Theorem 1: exact comparison, including a directional-loss constraint

Let \(Z(t)=X(t)-X_*\), and \(Y_s=(Y+Y^T)/2\). Then

\[
 \boxed{Y_*-Y_s=\langle Z(t)^TA(t)Z(t)\rangle\succeq0.}
 \tag{3}
\]

On \(\mathbf1^\perp\), where Y_* is invertible, there is also the stronger
constraint

\[
 \boxed{Y^TY_*^{-1}Y\preceq Y_s.}
 \tag{4}
\]

In (4), restrict both matrices to the contrast space before taking the inverse.
Equivalently one may use the Moore-Penrose inverse on t

## Scope

Consider any finite number of fixed-temperature terminals and internal thermal
stores. Every internal node v has a **constant positive scalar capacity** C_v.
Every edge has a bounded nonnegative reciprocal conductance g_uv(t)=g_vu(t),
piecewise continuous and periodic with finite period P. There is no advection,
coherent-wave interference, internal source, temperature-dependent controller,
capacity modulation or reset. Assume the averaged graph grounds every internal
component at a terminal, so the stable periodic solution is unique.

Let qbar=Y theta be its period-averaged terminal-current response, with current
positive into the network. Let G_union contain an edge exactly when its integrated
conductance over a period is positive. A terminal-avoiding path from i to j may
have arbitrary internal vertices, but no other terminal as an intermediate
vertex. Fixed-temperature terminals absorb a perturbation and are not transit
storage nodes.

Let I denote the set of internal vertices. The stage1 static-comparator theorems allow a general constant SPD storage matrix.
The result here requires diagonal positive capacities. This restriction is
essential to the positive-system proof and is not silently extended to the
larger algebraic class.

## Theorem

For any distinct terminals i and j:

1. Y_ji<=0.
2. Y_ji<0 if and only if there is a terminal-avoiding path from i to j in G_union.
3. In particular, Y_ji=0 if and only if Y_ij=0. The terminal response has exactly
   the same off-diagonal zero pattern as the static Kron reduction of the union
   graph, although its nonzero coefficients can be strongly unequal.

Consequently, a finite circuit in this class cannot have nonzero forward DC
transfer with exactly zero reverse DC transfer. Adding more finite stores,
more finite conductance phases or zero off-state contacts cannot change that
statement. It does not prohibit large **finite** isolation ratios.

## Q42

**Original versus reviewed claim.** The initial operation was useful DC directional routing through scheduled reciprocal contacts on fixed capacities. The first two-phase commutator construction fails: nonsymmetric sampled evolution does not imply nonsymmetric DC terminal response. The three-contact replacement does construct a nonreciprocal period-averaged matrix in the stated circuit model. It does not supply an assembled, resource-accounted thermal device.

**Proof audit.** In [Q42/PROOF.md, Theorems 1–2 and construction](../../review_material/Q42/stage1/PROOF.md), I reconstructed the periodic storage cancellation, expansion about the averaged graph's harmonic extension, integrated energy-form Cauchy–Schwarz, reversal adjoint and cyclic scalar contact recurrence. They support both `Y_* - sym(Y) >= 0` and `Y^T Y_*^(-1) Y <= sym(Y)` on contrasts, the two-phase impossibility, arbitrary positive unequal-contact formula and equal-duty finite-leakage formula. The continuum energy argument is consistent with its stated elliptic/admissible-trace assumptions. The comparison requires an admissible mean-conductance resource set; it does not settle nonconvex actuator/material budgets, transient cold preparation or all distinct-temperature currents individually.

**Independent checks.** A separate adaptive ODE period-map/current solver checks twelve fresh switched graphs, including singular individual phases and dense positive-definite capacity matrices. Maximum gap-identity/reversal errors are `9.18e-14`/`1.17e-13`; all circle-bound eigenvalues are positive in these cases. Four independently integrated ideal/leaky circulators match the formulas within `7.80e-14`. Full supplied solver and ordinary-controller replays pass. The ordinary schedule optimizer achieves directional excess `0.107633302232 G` against the construction's `0.107633302255 G`, and the uniform static star is analytically optimal for worst-hot-port cooling at the same mean total conductance. Thus the proposed generic cooling gain is decisively blocked, without denying useful routing.

**Prior operation and disposition.** The primary [Ju et al. abstract](https://advanced.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1002/adma.202309835) reports experimentally validated three-port convection-based thermal circulation.
